# Directional cap shadows and the section zonotope of a normal-preserving stress

This gives a concrete directional restriction on an ACTUAL ordinary cap stress. It uses the same allocated boundary and section measures, including inside and outside supporting facets. It neither partitions the base into contact cells nor substitutes a uniform lower-dimensional law for the inherited boundary profile.

The main outcome is the exact shadow identity (5) and the projection-body inclusion (7). Their canonical simplex calibration exposes a factor-d loss if one keeps only the resulting scalar section bound. No Gamma payment or arithmetic induction is claimed.

## 1. Actual stress and consistent selectors

Let K_z be positive compact convex bodies at finitely many actual sampled bases. Let eta denote the sum of their boundary measures, n_z the regular outer continuous normal, and

    H_j={a_j.z+u_j.X>=c_j},  theta_j>=0, sum_j theta_j=1.

For u_j nonzero retain an actual consistent body selector s_j(z,X) in [0,1] and section allocation lambda_j of total coarea T_j. Thus proper sections are fully counted, strict captured/empty boundary points have their ordinary bits, and on a supporting facet:

* inside: body density alpha and section density 1−alpha;
* outside: body density alpha and section density alpha.

Section densities are measured with the factor 1/|u_j|. For a pure-base cap use its whole-fiber selectors and set T_j=0, u_j=0.

Put W=sum_j theta_j s_j. Assume the normal-localized affine equality of the actual stress. In particular, for every continuous scalar b on the unit normal sphere,

    integral_boundary (W−beta)b(n_z) dS=0.             (1)

This follows from the SAME normal-dependent physical cone by using the two signs of fields constant in the physical variables. No source centroid assertion or volume coupling is needed for the following theorem.

For a continuous unit direction e set

    B(e)=sum_z |proj_(e-perp) K_z|_(d−1)>0.            (2)

The standard Cauchy projection identity is used only in its elementary line-fiber form: for a positive convex K, almost every line parallel to e through its shadow has exactly two boundary endpoints, so the area formula gives `integral_boundary |e.n| dS=2|proj_(e-perp)K|`. This also applies to a positive cap body.

## 2. Allocated shadows and the exact all-status formula

Define B_j(e) by summing these contributions over sampled fibers:

* if K_z intersect H_j has positive d-volume, use its ordinary (d−1)-dimensional projected volume;
* if the cap is strictly empty or touches in a face of dimension below d−1, use zero;
* at an outside-supporting facet F, use its SELECTED projected area

      |e.u_j|/|u_j| integral_F alpha_j dS.

For d=1, projected volume is zero-dimensional counting volume, and the same definitions reduce to interval endpoints with their selected weights. Pure-base caps give the sum of the whole captured-fiber shadows.

Then the exact identity is

    2 B_j(e)=integral_boundary s_j |e.n_z| dS
                                      +|e.u_j| T_j.  (3)

For a proper positive cap, its boundary consists of the captured old boundary plus its new section, whose outer normal is −u_j/|u_j|. Cauchy's identity gives (3). If an inside supporting cap contains the whole body, its body and section allocations add pointwise to one on the supporting facet, so (3) still reconstructs the full old boundary and full shadow. For an outside supporting cap, both allocations equal alpha; the two terms on the right are equal and together give twice the selected facet shadow. Lower-dimensional touches contribute zero. This proves (3) without identifying a selected supporting shadow with the closed unallocated face projection.

The complementary cap has the body selector 1−s_j and the SAME section allocation: the inside/outside rules exchange correctly. Consequently

    B_j(e)+B_j^complement(e)=B(e)+|e.u_j| T_j.        (4)

Each allocated shadow lies between zero and B(e), and the selected section shadow lies inside its captured shadow. Hence `|e.u_j|T_j<=B_j(e)`; the analogous complement inequality also holds. These statements can also be checked directly in each of the statuses above.

## 3. Exact directional profile identity and its inequality

Multiply (3) by theta_j, sum, and use (1) with `b(n)=|e.n|`. Cauchy's identity for the full fibers gives

    sum_j theta_j B_j(e)
       =beta B(e)+(1/2)sum_j theta_j T_j |e.u_j|.      (5)

Thus the theta-average captured SHADOW fraction exceeds beta by an exactly identified nonnegative angular section reserve. Both the actual orientation of every cap and its same allocated coarea are retained.

Write R(e)=sum theta_j T_j |e.u_j|. Since the left side of (5) is at most B(e), and is at least R(e),

    R(e)<=2 min(beta,1−beta) B(e)  for every e.        (6)

In the bad-value range beta<1/2 the operative coefficient is 2 beta. Formula (6) also follows from the allocated constant-field Gauss–Green identity `integral s_j n=u_j T_j`, the triangle inequality, and (1); the shadow proof additionally identifies the exact reserve and its supporting-facet interpretation.

Define the centrally symmetric convex projection body Pi K by support function `h_(Pi K)(e)=|proj_(e-perp)K|`, equivalently one half of the integral of |e.n| against its surface-area measure. The zonotope with support function R is

    Z_sec=sum_j theta_j T_j [−u_j,u_j].

Then (6) is the actual geometric inclusion

    Z_sec subset 2 min(beta,1−beta) sum_z Pi K_z.      (7)

For a critical group whose common effective weights obey `theta_ij T_ij=kappa_i rho_ij`, its summand is `kappa_i sum_j rho_ij[−u_ij,u_ij]`. This preserves the selected group normal geometry rather than replacing it by a chosen source-normal normalization.

The result extends to an actual probability law of cap records with consistent joint body/section allocations: integrate (3) against that law. Bounded total coarea and bounded continuous normals make all terms finite, and Tonelli/dominated convergence justify the same formulas. No finite same-stress sub-selection is needed.

## 4. Angular integration and precise loss of information

Averaging (6) over the continuous unit sphere, with its normalized rotation-invariant law, cancels the common factor `E_e |e.u|/|u|`. It gives

    sum_j theta_j |u_j| T_j
                 <=min(beta,1−beta) sum_z surface_area(K_z).  (8)

The left side is the theta-average ACTUAL allocated section area. This scalar consequence is weaker than the full directional inclusion. Neither equation controls a dimension-reduced mixed cap volume by itself, since projection removes line-length information and an outside supporting selector remains a selected shadow density.

For the canonical centroid-cap law of a d-simplex, every captured cap is a homothetic simplex of ratio `a=d/(d+1)`. Its shadow therefore has ratio `a^(d−1)` in EVERY direction. The audited normal stress has beta=Gamma_d=a^d. Substituting into (5) yields

    R(e)/(2 B(e))=a^(d−1)−a^d=Gamma_d/d.             (9)

Thus keeping only the lower bound beta>=sup_e R(e)/(2B(e)) would recover Gamma_d/d on this sharp simplex calibration, losing a factor d for d>=2. One must retain additional profile or geometric information to recover Gamma_d. This is a specific calibration of (6), not a claim that the entire cap law or full normal stress lacks that information.

The universal coefficient two in (6) cannot be decreased. For a centrally symmetric box at its center take the two opposite caps `X_1>=0` and `X_1<=0`, each of weight 1/2. They are actual critical caps, W=beta=1/2 almost everywhere, and the identity boundary coupling is normal-preserving. In direction e=e_1 their sections have total weighted area equal to the full shadow B(e), so equality holds in (6). No bad-value property is asserted for this equality example.

## 5. What is new and what remains open

The archived stress supplies (1) and consistent Gauss–Green allocations. The new bounded consequence expresses them as an all-direction equality for actual cap shadows and an explicit section-zonotope/projection-body bound, including the previously delicate supporting statuses. It does not give a parity-efficient normal-face partition, identify a lower-dimensional critical menu, or produce the missing arithmetic factor. The exact factor-d simplex calibration prevents treating its scalar angular average as a sharp payment theorem.
